source.note: Anaphoric 'he, she, it (just mentioned)' (Lat. is ea id, Ved. ayám iyám idám, Goth. is). Ringe 2017 p. 56 prints the whole sg./pl. paradigm: i-grade in the acc. and ins. and in the fem./neut. nom. (íh₂, íd), but e-grade masc. nom. sg. éy and e-grade elsewhere. The masc. nom. sg. is not *h₁ís: Beekes 2011 §15.2.1 p. 227 notes that it used to be set up as *is, which cannot account for Ved. ayám, Av. aēm, while OE he, OHG er point to *(h₁)e; Mallory & Adams 2006 §24.2 write *h₁éi (whole paradigm checked against Ringe p. 56 on 2026-10-30, t037 review: every cell matches); initial h₁ after Beekes 2011 p. 229 and Mallory & Adams 2006 §24.2. Dual and fem. ins. sg. not reconstructed (Ringe '???'), left out. Ringe also gives an unaccented clitic use (pure anaphora), not modelled here.
